rationale: I read the complete held EO 9294 (8 FR 221, signed January 4, 1943, Further Defining the Functions and Duties of the Office of Defense Transportation): it defines 'local passenger transportation equipment' and adds to the ODT functions under EOs 8989, 9156 and 9214 the review and approval of contracts and advice on allocation of such equipment. It has no own term. I read the held full text of EO 9625 (10 FR 12073, signed September 21, 1945), titled 'Revoking Executive Order 9294 of January 4, 1943': 'it is ordered that Executive Order 9294 of January 4, 1943, further defining the functions and duties of the Office of Defense Transportation, be, and it is hereby, revoked.' That names EO 9294 by number, date and title and revokes the whole order, with no savings clause. D6 self-check: no held instrument amends EO 9294 before 1945. A search of the held full-run texts for '9294' finds EO 9625, a hash fragment in EO 13620, and plant-seizure orders of 1944-45 (EOs 9462, 9554, 9569, 9570, 9602, 9603, 9604) that cite EO 9294 among the ODT authorities; those rely on the order while it stood and do not amend, continue or revive it, and all predate EO 9625. No held later instrument names or restores EO 9294. The OFR note 'Revoked by: EO 9625, September 21, 1945' and the 1989 snapshot row (revoked, actor EO 9625) agree. Both history observations (the API catalog record and the S1989 row) were reviewed; the extra supporting API record is not part of the frozen observation set. Provisional NO hypothesis; the effective end (signing September 21, 1945) is not otherwise adjudicated.
